rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad you reached out — five hours a week of real data/analyst time is a lot more useful than most offers I get. Halcyon Threshold is still early (solo, evenings/weekends so far), so I want to be upfront: I'm not ready to put this fully public yet — I've got a work disclosure thing to sort out first, hopefully soon. But there's concrete, non-public work that could start now. The idea I'm most drawn to: nobody is independently tracking whether frontier AI labs actually disclose safety incidents the way they say they will, versus what a proposed new reporting rule (72-hour incident reporting, docket FMIR-2026-0042) would require. I'd like to build a small, honest public scorecard on that — methodology, a source list, and a first data pass, done quietly for now, published once I'm clear to put my name on it. If that's interesting, a good first task would be: help me build a source list (which labs, which public commitments/policies, where incidents or near-misses have been reported historically) and sanity-check a simple scoring methodology. Totally fine if this isn't the kind of thing you had in mind — tell me what you'd actually enjoy and we can shape it around that instead. Thanks again — talk soon, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to **Priya Raman** (private email, not public) with a concrete, specific ask tied to the project idea below, and flagged that the org isn't public-facing yet.
